metadata.name: fdisk
metadata.description: Partition table manipulator for MBR disks

installation.note: fdisk is typically available by default as part of util-linux

overview.summary: fdisk is an interactive partition table editor for MBR (MS-DOS) disks. It creates, deletes, and modifies partitions. For GPT disks or scripting, parted or gdisk are often preferred. Use with extreme care; mistakes can cause data loss.
when_to_use: Create or modify MBR partitions on a disk
Repartition a disk (back up data first)

syntax.description: fdisk DEVICE enters interactive mode. fdisk -l lists partition tables. Always specify the disk device (e.g., /dev/sda), not a partition.

options.description: List partition tables for specified devices (or all)

examples.title: List partition tables
examples.description: Show partition layout for all block devices

examples.title: Edit partition table
examples.description: Enter interactive mode for /dev/sdb (use m for help)
examples.use_case: Create or modify partitions (back up first)

common_pitfalls.description: Writing to the wrong device can destroy data (e.g., /dev/sda instead of /dev/sdb).
common_pitfalls.solution: Double-check the device with lsblk or fdisk -l; never use the system disk unless you intend to.

related_commands.description: GPT and scriptable partitioning; often preferred for new disks
